bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the optical dispenser salary

An **optical dispenser salary** depends on the award classification, experience, and whether you work full‑time, part‑time, or casually. Most optical dispensers are covered by the *Health Services Award*, which sets minimum hourly rates that are higher than the National Minimum Wage. To turn an hourly rate into an annual figure, you need a simple formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. This article explains that calculation, including the role of the 38‑hour week, fortnightly pay, casual loading, superannuation, and tax.

### The basic conversion: hourly to annual

Assume a standard full‑time week of 38 hours (the ordinary hours used by the Fair Work Act). Multiply your hourly rate by 38 to get your weekly pay, then by 52 for the annual gross. For example, if your optical dispenser rate is $30.00 per hour:

- Weekly: $30.00 × 38 = $1,140.00
- Annual: $1,140.00 × 52 = $59,280.00

If you are paid fortnightly, simply double the weekly figure: $1,140.00 × 2 = $2,280.00 per fortnight. This method assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, and no penalty rates or allowances. For a quick calculation, use [the timesheet](/), where you can enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading.

### National Minimum Wage vs award rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is **$26.44 per hour** (or $1,004.90 per 38‑hour week). This applies to award‑free employees. However, optical dispensers are covered by the Health Services Award, which sets higher minimum rates. For example, a Level 1 optical dispenser might earn around $28–$32 per hour depending on experience. Always check the current [pay guides](/blog) for the exact classification.

### Casual loading and superannuation

Casual employees receive a **25% loading** on top of the minimum hourly rate. For an optical dispenser on a $30.00 base rate, the casual rate is $37.50 per hour. **Important:** when using [the timesheet](/), enter the base rate *before* casual loading, then tick the casual checkbox. Never enter a rate that already includes loading.

Superannuation is paid **on top** of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. If your annual gross is $59,280, your employer contributes an extra $7,113.60 into super, making total remuneration $66,393.60. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

### Tax and take‑home pay

Your annual gross is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- Over $190,000: 45% on excess over $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as a guide). For a $59,280 gross, the tax estimate is:

- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201–$45,000: ($45,000 – $18,200) × 15% = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001–$59,280: ($59,280 – $45,000) × 30% = $4,284
- Total tax: $8,304
- Medicare: $59,280 × 2% = $1,185.60
- Net annual: $59,280 – $8,304 – $1,185.60 = $49,790.40

Use [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) for a more detailed estimate.

### Comparing with average earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full‑time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 in May 2026. That equates to an annual salary of about $108,352. Many optical dispensers earn below this average, especially at entry level. The Health Services Award ensures a minimum floor, but actual salaries can vary by employer and location. See [average pay](/topics/average-pay) for industry comparisons.

### Using the timesheet for your optical dispenser salary

Our [timesheet](/) lets you convert any hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Enter your base rate (e.g., $30.00), select 38 hours per week, and tick casual if applicable. The tool shows gross pay before tax and super, plus a super estimate. It’s a fast way to see what your optical dispenser salary looks like over a year.

### Key points to remember

- Always use the **award rate** for your classification, not the National Minimum Wage.
- The formula **hourly × 38 × 52** gives a standard full‑time annual gross.
- Fortnightly pay is weekly × 2.
- Casual loading is 25% on top of the base rate.
- Super is 12% paid on top, up to the cap.
- Tax and Medicare reduce your take‑home pay.

For the official minimum rates, refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) for the Health Services Award. If you have an enterprise agreement, those rates may differ.

### Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
